chunks: And in the narration of Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from him, peace be upon him, he said:
“The injured person is carried so that he may stone the Jamarāt, and the one afflicted with abdominal illness is stoned for on his behalf, and salat (prayer) is performed on his behalf.”

key_terms.الْجِمَارَ: the Jamarāt, the ritual stone-targets in hajj
key_terms.اَلْكَسِيرُ: the injured or physically broken person
key_terms.اَلْمَبْطُونُ: the one suffering from abdominal illness
key_terms.وَيُصَلَّى عَنْهُ: salat (prayer) is performed on his behalf
key_terms.يُرْمَى عَنْهُ: the stoning is performed on his behalf

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for an injured or severely ill person regarding stoning the Jamarāt during hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal guidance for those unable to personally perform certain rites during hajj due to physical incapacity. It distinguishes between one who can still participate with assistance and one whose condition requires the act to be performed on their behalf, showing facilitation in acts of worship.
